solution: The line direction \((3,-5,2)\) is perpendicular to the normal \((1,3,-\alpha)\): \(3-15-2\alpha=0\Rightarrow\alpha=-6\). The point \((2,1,-2)\) lies on the plane: \(2+3-\alpha(-2)+\beta=0\), i.e. \(5+2\alpha+\beta=0\); with \(\alpha=-6\), \(5-12+\beta=0\Rightarrow\beta=7\), so \((\alpha,\beta)=(-6,7)\). Matches option B.
note: wrote 2 + 3 + 12 + beta = 0 => beta = 7 (false; it is 5 - 12 + beta = 0) after a garbled 6beta + beta; rewritten. Key B unchanged.

solution: With \(a=(-3,4,-8)\), \(\vec d=(3,5,6)\), \(P-a=(1,0,3)\). \((P-a)\times\vec d=(-15,3,5)\), \(|(P-a)\times\vec d|=\sqrt{259}\), \(|\vec d|=\sqrt{70}\). Distance \(=\dfrac{\sqrt{259}}{\sqrt{70}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{37}{10}}\). Matches option B.
note: cross product written (-15, -3, 5); it is (-15, 3, 5). Length and key B unchanged.

solution: Take \(A\) as the origin, \(B=(10,0,0)\), the floor in the \(xy\)-plane and height \(h\), so \(G=(10,10,h)\) and \(H=(0,10,h)\). Then \(\overrightarrow{AG}=10\hat{i}+10\hat{j}+h\hat{k}\) and \(\overrightarrow{BH}=-10\hat{i}+10\hat{j}+h\hat{k}\), so \(\cos\theta=\dfrac{\overrightarrow{AG}\cdot\overrightarrow{BH}}{|\overrightarrow{AG}||\overrightarrow{BH}|}=\dfrac{h^{2}}{h^{2}+200}=\dfrac{1}{5}\). Hence \(5h^{2}=h^{2}+200\), \(h^{2}=50\) and \(h=5\sqrt{2}\).
note: labels A(j), H(j + 10k) contradicted the vectors used, and 4h^2 = 200 was written for h^2 = 50; rewritten with consistent coordinates. Key D unchanged.

solution: A \((1,2,3)\), B \((2,3,4)\). Equation of line \(AB\): \[\frac{x - 1}{1} = \frac{y - 2}{1} = \frac{z - 3}{1}\] Given line \[\frac{x - 1}{2} = \frac{y + 1}{- 1} = \frac{z - 2}{0}\] shortest distance \(= \left| \frac{\left( {\overrightarrow{a}}_{2} - {\overrightarrow{a}}_{1} \right) \cdot \left( {\overrightarrow{b}}_{1} \times {\overrightarrow{b}}_{2} \right)}{\left| {\overrightarrow{b}}_{1} \times {\overrightarrow{b}}_{2} \right|} \right|\) \[= \left| \frac{(-3\widehat{j} - \widehat{k}) \cdot (\widehat{i} + 2\widehat{j} - 3\widehat{k})}{\sqrt{1 + 4 + 9}} \right| = \frac{|-6 + 3|}{\sqrt{14}}\] \[a = \frac{3}{\sqrt{14}}\] \[28a^{2} = 28 \times \frac{9}{14} = 18\]
note: a2 - a1 was written (0, 3, -1) (giving 9, not 3); it is (0, -3, -1). Answer 18 unchanged.

solution: Centroid \(G=\frac{P+Q+R}{3}\), with \(P+Q=2M=(4,2,4)\), \(R(-1,4,2)\Rightarrow G=(1,2,2)\). The two lines are \((2,2s,-3-s)\) and \((1+t,-3-3t,-1+t)\); equal \(x\) gives \(t=1\), then \(2s=-6\Rightarrow s=-3\), and both give \((2,-6,0)\). Distance \(=\sqrt{1+64+4}=\sqrt{69}.\)
note: parameters written s = 1, t = -3 (they do not give (2, -6, 0)); they are s = -3, t = 1. Key C unchanged.

solution: Required equation of plane \[P_{1} + \lambda P_{2} = 0\] \[(x - y - z - 1) + \lambda(2x + y - 3z + 4) = 0\] Given that its distance from the origin is \(\sqrt{\frac{2}{21}}\): \(\frac{|4\lambda - 1|}{\sqrt{(2\lambda + 1)^{2} + (\lambda - 1)^{2} + ( - 3\lambda - 1)^{2}}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{21}}\) \[\Rightarrow 21(4\lambda - 1)^{2} = 2\left( 14\lambda^{2} + 8\lambda + 3 \right)\] \[\Rightarrow 336\lambda^{2} - 168\lambda + 21 = 28\lambda^{2} + 16\lambda + 6\] \[\Rightarrow 308\lambda^{2} - 184\lambda + 15 = 0\] \[\Rightarrow 308\lambda^{2} - 154\lambda - 30\lambda + 15 = 0\] \[\Rightarrow (2\lambda - 1)(154\lambda - 15) = 0\] \(\Rightarrow \lambda = \frac{1}{2}\) or \(\frac{15}{154}\); for \(\lambda = \frac{1}{2}\) the required plane is \[4x - y - 5z + 2 = 0\]
note: the distance was written 2/sqrt21; it is sqrt(2/21), as used in the next line. Key D unchanged.

solution: The line is \(3y - 2z - 1 = 0 = 3x - z + 4\). The planes have normals \((0,3,-2)\) and \((3,0,-1)\). If the line's direction ratios are \(a, b, c\), then \(3b - 2c = 0\) and \(3a - c = 0\), so \(6a = 3b = 2c\) and \(a:b:c = 1:2:3\). The point \((-1,1,1)\) lies on both planes, so any point of the line is \((3K - 1, 6K + 1, 9K + 1)\). For the foot from \((2,-1,6)\): \(3(3K - 3) + 6(6K + 2) + 9(9K - 5) = 0\Rightarrow 126K = 42\Rightarrow K = \frac{1}{3}\), giving the foot \((0,3,4)\). Distance \(= \sqrt{4 + 16 + 4} = 2\sqrt{6}\).
note: the perpendicularity equation did not subtract the given point (it was 3(3K-1) + 6(6K+1) + 9(9K+1) = 0) and the second normal was written (3, -1, 0); rewritten. K = 1/3 and key C unchanged.

solution: For \(L_{1}:\frac{x - 1}{2} = \frac{y - 2}{3} = \frac{z - 3}{4}\) and \(L_{2}:\frac{x}{1} = \frac{y}{\alpha} = \frac{z - 5}{1}\), \(\vec{n} = (2,3,4)\times(1,\alpha,1) = (3 - 4\alpha)\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + (2\alpha - 3)\hat{k}\). With \(\overrightarrow{BA} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}\), the shortest distance is \(\left|\frac{\overrightarrow{BA}\cdot\vec{n}}{|\vec{n}|}\right| = \frac{|13 - 8\alpha|}{\sqrt{(4\alpha - 3)^{2} + 4 + (2\alpha - 3)^{2}}} = \frac{5}{\sqrt{6}}\). So \(6(64\alpha^{2} - 208\alpha + 169) = 25(20\alpha^{2} - 36\alpha + 22)\), i.e. \(116\alpha^{2} + 348\alpha - 464 = 0\), and \(\alpha_{1} + \alpha_{2} = \frac{-348}{116} = -3\).
note: |n|^2 used +16 for the j component (it is 2, so +4), giving expansion errors (-280 alpha, 34, -164); corrected to -208 alpha, 22, -464. Sum -3 and key D unchanged.
